title: Chaman Prakash v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J. and Dinesh Pathak, J.
disposition: Representation to be heard; recovery stayed four weeks.
headnote: A theft FIR under section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 does not permit the licensee to treat a provisional assessment as the final demand without a hearing. Clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the theft procedure for inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment; the course adopted was dehors section 126 and clauses 6.8/8.1. The consumer cannot be compelled to deposit on the provisional figure. The writ was disposed of without merits, directing a speaking decision on the representation after hearing, with the recovery notice kept in abeyance meantime.
facts: After an FIR under section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 alleging theft, the licensee issued a 14 September 2020 provisional assessment and a 16 October 2020 recovery notice demanding Rs 1,26,457 from Chaman Prakash. He said the checking report and provisional assessment were never served; he learned of the demand from the recovery notice and made a representation on 5 January 2021. The Power Corporation did not dispute that final assessment was made without a hearing.

reusable_constructions.construction: A provisional assessment cannot be treated as the final assessment, and the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the provisional amount, unless a final assessment is made after considering objections and affording a hearing.
Clause 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the procedure for inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment in a case of theft of electricity.

holding_units.holding: Where assessment follows a section 135 theft FIR, treating the provisional assessment as the final demand without a hearing is dehors section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and clauses 6.8/8.1 of the Supply Code, 2005. Clause 8.1 requires inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment. The consumer cannot be compelled to deposit on the provisional figure. The licensee was directed to decide the representation by a speaking order after hearing; the recovery notice was kept in abeyance for four weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier.

principle_tags.application: The demand arose from an FIR under section 135, but the assessment and recovery still had to follow section 126 and clause 8.1: a hearing before any final assessment, and no compulsion to deposit the provisional amount.

lead_authorities.name: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

not_decided.point: merits of the theft allegation and quantum of the assessment
not_decided.note: Writ disposed of without entering into the merits; the licensee was directed to decide the representation after hearing.

authorities.name: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
authorities.proposition: Without a final assessment after considering objections and giving an opportunity of hearing, the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the provisional amount; notices founded only on the provisional assessment are unsustainable.
